note: Subjects/Maths/M1 Mechanics 1/1 Mathematical models in mechanics.md
outline: Mechanics replaces objects and contacts with idealised models. A particle has mass but negligible size; a lamina has negligible thickness; a rigid body does not deform. Light means negligible mass, uniform means evenly distributed mass, and inextensible means fixed length. Smooth contact has no friction, while rough contact may have friction. A light smooth pulley with a light string gives equal tension on both sides. A bead is constrained to a wire; a peg is a fixed support. Choose each assumption for the property relevant to the problem.

misconceptions.refutation: A particle has mass, but its dimensions are negligible for the problem.
misconceptions.contrast: A vehicle can be treated as a particle when only its motion along a route matters.

misconceptions.statement: A light rod or string has zero tension or force.
misconceptions.refutation: Light means its mass is negligible; it can still transmit a force.
misconceptions.contrast: A light string can pull with non-zero tension.

misconceptions.statement: A smooth surface or pulley has no normal reaction or tension.
misconceptions.refutation: Smooth removes friction, not the normal reaction or the tension in a string.
misconceptions.contrast: A block on a smooth table still experiences a normal reaction.

misconceptions.statement: Uniform means the same as light or rigid.
misconceptions.refutation: Uniform describes even mass distribution; light describes negligible mass and rigid describes no deformation.
misconceptions.contrast: A uniform heavy rod may be rigid and has its centre of mass at its midpoint.

misconceptions.statement: Inextensible means the string cannot move.
misconceptions.refutation: Its length stays constant; different parts can still move.
misconceptions.contrast: For a taut inextensible string over a fixed pulley, connected particles have equal displacement magnitudes.

items.stem: Explain the modelling assumptions needed to use equal tension on both sides of a pulley in a connected-particle problem.

rubric.point: The string is light, so its mass is negligible.
The pulley is smooth, so friction at contact is neglected.

items.stem: Explain whether a rough wire guarantees friction acts on a stationary bead, and give a reason.

rubric.point: Roughness permits friction but does not guarantee a non-zero friction force.
Friction depends on the tendency for relative motion.

items.explanation: Rough means friction is available. If there is no tendency to slip along the wire, the friction force can be zero.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: A car is driven along a straight road. Explain why the car can be modelled as a particle when finding the time for the journey, but not when investigating the turning of its wheels.

rubric.point: For the journey the car's dimensions are negligible compared with the distance travelled, so its size and shape do not affect the motion along the road.
Its mass is kept, so weight, driving force and resistance can still be applied at the single point.
A particle has no dimensions, so it cannot rotate; the wheels need a model with size and mass distribution, such as a rigid body.

items.explanation: Modelling as a particle neglects dimensions, not mass: along a straight road only the position of one point matters, so the journey time is unaffected. Rotation is a property of an extended body, so a point with no size cannot represent a spinning wheel; a rigid body model is needed instead.
hints: Decide which property of the car the particle model throws away, and which it keeps.
Compare the size of the car with the length of the journey.
Ask what a single point with no dimensions is unable to do.

items.stem: A small metal ring slides along a fixed straight horizontal wire. The ring is modelled as a bead and the wire is modelled as smooth. Explain what each of these two assumptions means for the forces on the ring and for its motion.

rubric.point: Bead: the ring's dimensions are negligible and it is threaded on the wire, so it is constrained to move along the wire and cannot leave it.
Smooth: there is no friction at the contact, so no force along the wire opposes the sliding.
A normal reaction perpendicular to the wire still acts, so smoothness does not remove all contact force.

items.explanation: Bead removes the ring's size and fixes it on the wire, so its motion is one-dimensional along the wire. Smooth removes only the tangential friction; the wire still pushes on the ring with a normal reaction perpendicular to it, which is what supports the ring's weight.
hints: Take the two words one at a time and name the property each one neglects.
Decide in which direction the contact force can act once friction is removed.
Ask what holds the ring up if there is no friction along the wire.

items.stem: A diving board is fixed at one end and is modelled as a uniform rigid rod. Find the statement that follows from this model.

options.A: Its weight acts at its midpoint and its shape does not change under the forces.
options.B: Its weight is negligible, so only the diver's weight acts on it.
options.C: No friction can act where the board is supported.
options.D: It has mass but no length, so it cannot turn about its support.

items.explanation: Uniform means the mass is evenly distributed, so the weight acts at the midpoint, and rigid means the board keeps its shape under the forces. Uniform and rigid say nothing about how much mass there is, about friction at the support, or about the board's length: a rod keeps its length.
hints: Translate each of the two words in the model into one consequence.
Check whether each statement is about mass distribution, amount of mass, friction or size.
A rod model keeps one dimension: its length.

flashcards.back: A body with mass whose dimensions are negligible in the problem.
A flat sheet whose thickness is negligible compared with its other dimensions.
A body whose shape and size do not change under the forces considered.

flashcards.front: What do light, uniform and non-uniform mean for a rod?
flashcards.back: Light: negligible mass. Uniform: mass evenly distributed along its length. Non-uniform: mass not evenly distributed.

flashcards.front: What is a light inextensible string?
flashcards.back: A string with negligible mass whose length remains constant when taut.

flashcards.front: What is a smooth surface? What is a rough surface?
flashcards.back: A smooth surface exerts no friction; a rough surface may exert friction.

flashcards.front: What is a light smooth pulley?
flashcards.back: A pulley of negligible mass with no friction at the string contact; for a light string, tension is equal on both sides.

flashcards.front: What are a bead, wire and peg in mechanics?
flashcards.back: A bead is a small object constrained to move on a wire. A wire provides its path. A peg is a fixed small support around which a string may pass.

M1-1.1.motivate: A real car has size, a rope stretches a little, and a wheel has friction. A useful mechanics model keeps the properties that affect the question. Which of these details can you ignore in a particular calculation?

discover.stem: A light inextensible string passes over a smooth pulley. Which conclusion follows from the model?

options.A: The string has no tension because it is light.
options.B: The taut string keeps a constant length and can carry tension.
options.C: The string cannot move because it is inextensible.
options.D: The pulley cannot exert any contact force because it is smooth.

discover.explanation: Light means negligible string mass, while inextensible means constant length when taut. Smooth removes friction at contact, not tension or the contact force.

M1-1.1.establish: A particle has mass but negligible dimensions. A lamina is a flat sheet of negligible thickness. A rigid body does not change shape or size under the forces considered. A light rod or string has negligible mass; light does not mean unable to transmit force. A uniform rod has mass evenly distributed along its length and, in uniform gravity, its centre of mass is at the midpoint. A non-uniform rod has uneven mass distribution. An inextensible string keeps a constant length when taut, so connected particles have linked displacements. A smooth surface has no friction but can exert a normal reaction; a rough surface may exert friction. A light smooth pulley has negligible mass and no friction at the string contact; with a light string, tension is equal on both sides. A bead is a small object constrained to move along a wire. A wire defines its path; a peg is a fixed small support around which a string can pass. A peg or wire needs a stated smoothness assumption before friction is ignored.
M1-1.1.connect: In a later connected-particle problem, first use inextensibility to link motion, then use the light string and smooth pulley to link tensions. For a rod in a moments problem, uniformity determines where its weight acts; rigidity only tells you its shape stays fixed.
M1-1.1.note:
- Particle: mass retained, size negligible; lamina: negligible thickness; rigid body: no deformation.
- Light: negligible mass; uniform: evenly distributed mass; non-uniform: uneven mass distribution.
- Inextensible: constant taut length; smooth: no friction; rough: friction may act.
- Light smooth pulley with light string: equal tensions on both sides.
- Bead: small object constrained to a wire; peg: fixed support for a string.
M1-1.1.self_explain: A uniform rod rests on a smooth table. Which assumption places its weight at the midpoint, and which removes friction? Explain why the table can still exert a normal reaction.
M1-1.1.plain_words: A model is a useful simplification of a real object. First say what you want to predict; then keep the properties that affect that prediction. For each assumption, give its meaning, what it lets you do, and a circumstance in which it would stop being useful. No algebra is needed here: begin with mass, size, shape, contact and length. Mass is the amount of matter; weight is the gravitational force on it. A force is a push or pull, and rotation means turning.

forms.name: Interpret an assumption in context
wordings: State what this modelling assumption means.
Explain how the stated assumption simplifies this situation.

forms.example:
A bead slides along a smooth fixed wire while pulled by a light taut string passing over a smooth fixed peg. Explain the models.
1. Name the objects: bead, wire, string and peg. The bead is small and its path is constrained by the wire.
2. Translate each adjective: smooth wire removes friction there, but a normal reaction can still act; light string removes its own mass, not its tension.
3. Identify the support: the fixed peg provides a place for the string to change direction.
4. Compare another light object: a light rod can transmit force even though its own weight is neglected.
forms.check: A uniform rigid beam rests on a rough horizontal support. State what uniform, rigid and rough each mean for this beam. Must the friction force be non-zero? Explain.
forms.answer: Uniform means mass is evenly distributed along the beam; for a straight beam its centre of mass is at its midpoint. Rigid means its shape and size do not change under the forces considered. Rough means friction may act at the support. Non-zero friction is not guaranteed: if there is no tendency to slip, no friction is needed.

rubric.point: Uniform means mass is evenly distributed along the beam, equivalently constant mass per unit length; midpoint centre of mass alone is insufficient.
The beam does not deform under the forces considered.
Rough contact permits friction but does not guarantee non-zero friction; explains this through absence of slipping tendency or absence of a required tangential force.

retry.check: Two hanging loads are joined by a taut light inextensible string passing over a single fixed light smooth pulley, with straight vertical ends. Explain separately what permits equal tension magnitudes and what links the magnitudes of their displacements. Does either conclusion require equal load masses?
retry.answer: A taut light string over the ideal light smooth pulley permits equal tension magnitudes. Inextensibility fixes the string length; with this fixed pulley and straight taut ends, one segment lengthens by the amount the other shortens, giving equal displacement magnitudes. Neither result requires equal load masses.

rubric.point: Links equal tensions to the light string and smooth ideal pulley, rather than to inextensibility.

Links equal displacement magnitudes to the constant length of the taut inextensible string in the stated fixed-pulley arrangement; credit an explanation that one load/end rises by the same distance that the other falls, without requiring the word segment or a repetition of fixed.
Neither conclusion requires equal masses.

forms.example:
A delivery van travels between two towns. Later an engineer asks whether it might tip while turning. Compare treating the van as a particle.
1. Set the target: for journey time from a specified speed and route distance, changes in the van position matter and its dimensions can be ignored relative to the journey. Its mass is retained.
2. Give the useful consequence: one point represents the van in the translation model; no description of its orientation is needed for that calculation.
3. Change the target: tipping depends on the dimensions, centre-of-mass position and support contacts, so a particle model loses information needed about rotation.
4. Refine only as needed: a rigid-body model with finite size is a possible improvement for tipping if deformation is negligible. If bending or deformation mattered, rigidity would itself need review. These are contextual modelling choices, not a requirement to calculate vehicle tipping in this chapter.
forms.check: A modeller treats a loaded diving board as a rigid body to estimate its position before anyone jumps. State the assumption, explain its simplifying consequence, and give one context-specific limitation and a possible refinement if observed behaviour contradicts it.
forms.answer: The board is assumed not to change shape or size under the load. It can be represented by a fixed geometry instead of calculating bending. A real diving board may bend appreciably when loaded, changing its shape or tip position; a deformable or elastic-board model could include that deflection. Credit any other physically valid limitation linked to the stated assumption and an appropriate refinement; a rigid body need not be stationary.

rubric.point: States the rigid-body assumption as no deformation under the load: shape and size remain unchanged, equivalently distances between material points remain constant. Accept the contextual wording that the board does not change shape or size; rigidity does not imply that the board is stationary.

retry.check: A thin flat metal sign rotates about a hinge. Choose between a particle model and a rigid lamina model when the sign dimensions affect its turning. State one assumption, its useful consequence, and a context-specific limitation with a possible refinement.
retry.answer: A rigid lamina is suitable if the sign remains flat, does not deform and its thickness is negligible compared with its width and height. Its in-plane dimensions are retained for turning while thickness or deformation can be ignored. A particle would discard the dimensions needed here. If the sign bends noticeably, a deformable sheet would be a possible refinement; if its thickness matters, retain a three-dimensional rigid body. Credit either limitation with its matching refinement or another valid context-specific pair.

rubric.point: Chooses a rigid lamina and gives a relevant assumption: negligible thickness or no deformation.

Links the model to retaining dimensions or distances from the hinge needed for turning while simplifying thickness or deformation; accept an explanation that the distances from the hinge are retained.

Identifies failure of an assumption for this sign: appreciable bending/deformation, or thickness significant enough to affect the turning calculation. Negligible thickness or no deformation states an assumption, not a limitation.

Explicitly refines the model to address the stated failure: bending requires a deformable/elastic/flexible sheet or plate that allows deformation; significant thickness requires a three-dimensional body retaining thickness. Credit a physically valid matching pair only; thickness alone, negligible thickness, or an unrelated refinement earns no credit. Accept equivalent hyphenated wording and descriptions with intervening adjectives, such as a deformable elastic-sheet model or a deformable thin metal sheet, when the proposed sheet or plate model allows the stated bending; do not require an exact contiguous phrase. Continue to require a physically valid limitation/refinement pair. An elastic model or a model that allows bending earns refinement credit only when explicitly proposed to represent the stated bending or deformation of this sign; merely mentioning elasticity, or proposing an elastic model for a significant-thickness limitation without retaining thickness, earns no refinement credit.

misconceptions.temptation: A dot looks like nothing is there.
misconceptions.fix: Neglect dimensions only; keep the mass.

misconceptions.idea: Light means no force can be transmitted.
misconceptions.temptation: Negligible mass sounds like negligible force.
misconceptions.fix: Ignore the component own weight; a string can still pull and a rod can still transmit force.

misconceptions.temptation: Friction is the most familiar contact force.
misconceptions.fix: Remove friction only; keep the normal reaction or the relevant string tension. Conversely, roughness permits friction but does not guarantee a non-zero value; ask whether slipping occurs or tends to occur.

misconceptions.idea: Uniform, rigid and light are interchangeable.
misconceptions.temptation: All three sound like simplifying adjectives.
misconceptions.fix: Separate mass distribution, deformation and negligible mass.

misconceptions.idea: Inextensible means the string cannot move, or by itself determines all motion and tension properties.
misconceptions.temptation: Several assumptions often appear in the same sentence.
misconceptions.fix: Use the light string and smooth ideal pulley for tension; for the usual equal end motions also require a taut inextensible string, one fixed pulley and the stated fixed path.
